items.title: Johnny DeDroit Interview, 1969-12-04
items.q: So they heard me playing down in the pit and they came to me and said, will you go with us on the interstate second? ... we want you for one reason. In the middle of our act, as you know, instead of the violinist, we want you to fill that spot.

ctx.x: I've seen some of those recordings with Johnson. Did you solo with him? Can you hear yourself on him? No.

No. We had another fellow from the Russian Symphony, Eisenhower. He played lead trumpet and I played hop trumpet. But I will say that I created more attention than he did because I get up and take a chorus and it was absolutely strange to their ears. I toured the, they offered the theater clothes with an act called Adelaide Hughes. I don't know whether you remember that. They were two of the greatest dancers that ever lived.
